hypothesis: The model-resolve-cache record's reported-only finding #2 (20260927-013300): 'the warm-turn ack->user_row spread includes the durable-append fdatasync - flush-regime sensitive per the fleet advisory'. The warmturn-fdatasync lane's honest negative (20260929-161500) characterized the spread through trap-episode windows on a host that per the hostregime census v1.2 was NOT in a census state (its preflight A-class sat 26-28ms in episodes), so the spread's REGIME axis was never measured: nobody has measured the in-product warm-turn rows across LABELED census states. The unlock: the hostregime census (712223f) is the regime-label authority (fresh bench-class hosts run fast 0.84-0.90 / slow 2.04-2.10ms; repeat-fsync flat in ALL regimes) and the corrected dual-class preflight identifies the state at every leg boundary. Paired question: does the warm-turn append path pay the fresh-write class (state-sensitive) or the repeat-fsync class (state-invariant)? Pre-registered predictions: P1 the in-product session-row fdatasync stays in its sub-ms band in BOTH census states (slow/fast ratio <1.5x; no correlation with the A-class p50) = repeat-fsync-class pricing, closing the finding as an honest negative with the mechanism named; P2 the sidecar isolated product-shape probe replicates the census's flat append_fsync class; P3 the A-class flips between the census bands in-battery; P4 the volume term lifts with regime only at the multi-MB end; P5 the journal checkpoint (the phase's first sync) carries the trap exposure while the per-row syncs do not.
approach: Characterization-only (no code change, no branch, no PR): one fresh bench-class VM (hillclimb-perf-warmturn-fdatasync-spread, ubuntu:22.04 16c/32GB/40GB), one release build at the pinned tip cca05169d (origin/main; the named tip; verified: append_cached per-row sync_data + batched journal append_records both present), 20 sequential strace-censused trials in 3 interleaved arms ([f,r,g] x4 then r x8), the corrected probe12 dual-class preflight at EVERY leg boundary (40 ISOLATED fresh+sync_all+rename @0.5s + 20 repeat-fsync with the prior lane's pre-sync+12s-settle B-artifact fix, + the v1.2 census-state labeler: CENSUS-FAST/CENSUS-SLOW bands from the hostregime census, FLEET-PHASE by rule-B repeat>2x, DEEP-SUSPECT fresh>4x floor with B flat), a continuous sidecar isolated product-shape probe (open O_APPEND+4KB write+fdatasync @2s), a state-gated isolated volume probe (4K/64K/512K/4M/16M x 20 ops @0.5s), and post-battery triage (a fresh-file incremental-growth test at the sidecar cadence + a size ladder). ARMS: f1-f4 fresh mock sessions (the wave-5 msgsettle protocol verbatim: 120x40 PTY, probe-input-ready, typed prompt, Enter->first-chunk ack, needle+600ms-stability settle; 4 turns, 3 warm); r1-r12 the bench-repo real-session fixture session-imageheavy-vizbuilder.jsonl (22.9MB/6870 rows, sha f6ab958a) RESUMED with the settled copy (production shape) x3 warm turns; g1-g4 fresh mock sessions on a big-reply script carrying IN-PRODUCT 65,552B and 524,306B assistant rows (tail-marker needles: the reply head scrolls out of the viewport mid-stream). Every trial: PI_REQUEST_TIMING on, strace -f -tt -T -y lean filter on the daemon, per-row write-size join (each sync paired with the preceding write() bytes on the same fd), binary+fixture sha asserted, mock request-count parity (one completion POST per turn).
parity_notes: No product code changed (characterization-only): frozen surfaces untouched by construction. The tip's warm-turn durable-append path verified by code read at cca05169d: session rows append via window_cache.rs append_cached (open O_APPEND + write_all + flush + sync_data per row - the deliberate #2545/#3023 strengthening, unchanged); the journal checkpoint is the batched append_records (one sync_all per checkpoint, #2936's shape, unchanged). The TS-parity analysis is carried verbatim from the prior warmturn-fdatasync record (20260929-161500): TS session rows are plain appendFileSync with zero durability syncs; the port's per-row fdatasync is the disclosed strengthening; the parity-restoring cut remains the operator's contract call, twice recorded - this census does not touch it. The measured mock path replicates the campaign's compare.msg_send provider path (bench vendored mock_provider SSE, queue-matched).

measurements.headline: THE PAIRED QUESTION ANSWERED: the warm-turn durable-append path prices like the REPEAT-FSYNC class. The in-product session-row fdatasync held its 0.40-0.54ms p50 band through a 41x fresh-create swing (CENSUS-FAST legs A 0.85-1.02 vs DEEP-SUSPECT legs A 24.4-34.8ms; correlation session-vs-A = 0.064), with the journal checkpoint equally flat (0.67/0.69ms) and the trap exposure concentrated on the phase's first sync exactly as the prior lane found. The mechanism: the state machine's lift is a fresh-file-create+metadata effect (the census class table: fresh4k/64k lift 0.75->1.79 / 0.79->1.81, fresh256k flat, append_fsync flat 0.60/0.59, repeat-fsync flat 0.54/0.53); the per-row append touches no file creation - its only disk work is flushing the new row's KB-class dirty block, which prices at the flat repeat-sync floor. The finding closes as an honest negative WITH the mechanism named, and the prior lane's negative STANDS on the production surface. The spread's real members: (1) the op-size quantum (>=64KB rows carry ~27-30ms on this host, state-independent - the big-paste/tool-result row class); (2) the first-sync trap (the journal checkpoint, regime-class traps to 67ms); (3) the instrument's own isolated-probe regime (the sidecar's 66-minute sustained 26-31ms window that the production surface never felt).

(3) The big-reply arm's settle misses were a needle-shape artifact (the reply head scrolls out of the 40-line viewport mid-stream): tail markers as needles - all g-trials completed 4/4 after. The analyzer was validated BEFORE the campaign on the prior lane's raw strace (reproduced its published sub-ms session band, the journal trap pierce, and the 26-28ms create-path class; 3 parser bugs found and fixed: the -T seconds->ms unit, the resumed-line timestamp form, and the interrupted-write size join - the latter caught again by the served-path assertion on g2 and fixed before the final analysis).
